assessments.reasoning: The publisher-designated acquisition returned the complete LICENSE file at OpenLDAP commit 37b4b3f6cc4bf34e1d3dec61e69914b9819d8894. Its reported SHA-256 matches the claim's capture pin. The file contains the Version 1 notice dated 22 August 1998 and names Net Boolean Incorporated in the copyright line. The repository path establishes where this copy was retained. The notice supplies the edition and attribution.

The complete SPDX json/details/NBPL-1.0.json at data revision 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48 gives NBPL-1.0 as licenseId. Its decoded licenseText matches all 868 bounded tokens of the OpenLDAP capture in order. The comparison uses the decoded field, excluding the template, HTML, and metadata.
The complete SPDX text/NBPL-1.0.txt at the same data revision matches all 868 bounded tokens of the OpenLDAP capture in order. Its bounded text is byte-identical to the decoded SPDX licenseText.

challenge.method: Reopened the three designated sources in order. Checked where the notice begins and ends, compared the bounded token sequences and literal text, and examined whether the repository path, dated attribution, SPDX cross-reference, or template metadata supported a different reading of the edition or its historical scope.
challenge.results: Each bounded passage yielded the same ordered sequence of 868 tokens. The title, version date, Net Boolean Incorporated attribution, and closing marker agree. The OpenLDAP copy uses different line wrapping and indentation, so its bounded bytes differ from both SPDX representations. The SPDX cross-reference reports match=false for the historical Gitweb URL. It points to the same OpenLDAP commit and LICENSE path but supplies no explanation for that flag. The direct token comparison used the retained raw copy. None of the three acquisitions contained a Vixie Cron README header to strip or compare.

limitations: The assessment is limited to the captured Net Boolean Version 1 notice from its title through The End and the two SPDX files at the supplied data revision. The mapping from that revision to release 3.29.0 was supplied in the claim and was not independently checked against a release manifest.
The OpenLDAP capture and SPDX cross-reference document the historical copy. Direct publication by Net Boolean and applicability to other editions or files remain unverified.
The comparison establishes documentary correspondence. Legal equivalence, rights for other works, text reuse, installation, and Index lifecycle are outside its scope.
reasoning: The pinned SPDX detail record identifies NBPL-1.0. Comparing the title-through-The End passage from the OpenLDAP LICENSE against both fixed SPDX representations gave 868 matching tokens in order in each comparison. The comparison lowercased the text and used runs of ASCII letters or digits as tokens, leaving punctuation and line wrapping outside the comparison.
